newsitem.title: USA: FINEX defers Singapore dollar futures contract.
newsitem.headline: FINEX defers Singapore dollar futures contract.

text.p: FINEX, the financial products division of the New York Cotton Exchange, plans to launch its new Asian currency futures contracts in late June, but will omit the Singapore dollar contract from the launch, exchange officials said Monday.
"We were due to decide last week on a date for the launch of our Asian currency futures contracts," FINEX marketing director Charles Minaar told Reuters.

"We have some final details to work out with Asian authorities to do with settlement issues, but we are tentatively planning to launch the contracts on June 26, with the exception of the Singapore dollar contract."
FINEX has proposed contracts on the U.S. dollar/Malaysian ringgit, U.S. dollar/Indonesian rupiah, the U.S. dollar/Thai baht and the U.S. dollar/Singapore dollar.
Earlier the Malaysian Monetary Exchange signed an agreement with FINEX to allow it to trade selected FINEX currency futures and options on the floor of the Malaysian exchange.
"We have received CFTC (U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission) approval for the contracts, but have heard that the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has some reservations," Minaar said.
"We would like the MAS to express those concerns directly to FINEX so we could clear this matter up," he said.
The Monetary Authority of Singapore on June 2 told Reuters, in written response to questions, that it was concerned about any trading in the Singapore dollar that might destabilize the market.
Singapore has long restricted internationalization of its currency and keeps a tight rein on trading of the Singapore dollar. ((Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, 212-859-1641))
